tasks.short: Agree advertising themes, copy changes and expectations with the client.

steps.what: Read the current copy, product information and earlier client feedback.
Prepare questions and proposed discussion points.

loop.input: Reference pack and campaign brief.
loop.output: Discussion agenda with linked sources and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check source links, required brief fields and writer acceptance of proposed questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; missing sources become questions for the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the agenda, but interpreting free-text feedback needs a bounded reading step.

steps.what: Discuss themes, methods, disagreements and desired copy changes with the client.
Turn discussion notes into a revised brief and change list.

loop.input: Writer's discussion notes and existing campaign brief.
loop.output: Proposed brief changes, owners and unresolved decisions.
loop.check: Each change cites a note; uncertain agreement stays unresolved; writer checks completeness.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes express decisions indirectly; field copying cannot reliably distinguish suggestions from agreement.

steps.what: Approve the revised direction and requested copy changes.
Forward the approved brief and update the project record.

tasks.design: A brief workspace in the {DOCS} links approved product information and current copy, while a job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles references. Bounded loops prepare an agenda and proposed brief changes from the writer's notes; the client approves the changed direction in the {WORKFLOW}. Approval updates the {PROJECT} and notifies the marketing team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Context sits across documents and feedback threads. Templates can organise it, but interpreting comments and negotiating intent require people.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and brief templates are cheaper to build with coding assistance. Bounded extraction can prepare reviewable paperwork from free text.
tasks.still_hard: Unspoken expectations, conflicting stakeholders and unclear authority still require conversation. A polished summary can misstate agreement.
tasks.human_edge: The writer hears hesitation, challenges weak positioning and negotiates wording the client will support.

ambition.what: Resolve the target audience and single campaign promise at each brief review.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time reconstructing context and more time testing the client's reasoning. The change creates no automatic authority to approve campaign direction.

reach.task: Frame audience, campaign objective and success criteria before commissioning copy.
reach.learn: Campaign planning, audience prioritisation and the distinction between communication goals and business outcomes.

evidence.claim: Assisted business writing can reduce drafting time; this does not establish savings for client negotiation.
Source assembly, approval routing and project updates can use deterministic integrations and existing configuration.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: An internal marketing sponsor or external client approves the direction.
The reference pack uses current, permissioned material from the {DOCS}.
The preparation share is an explicit estimate; the supplied priors support keeping the central conversation human.
GDPR applies to personal data in notes. Applicable EU AI Act duties depend on downstream use.
Access estimates include a small pilot and any required consultation under national rules; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Who can approve a brief, and which changes require further approval?
Can the {DOCS}, {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW} expose version and permission information?
Do existing notes contain personal data or confidential client information?
Is consultation required under applicable national rules or workplace agreements?
research_questions: How reliably can the loop distinguish an agreed change from a suggestion in representative notes?
Which brief fields prevent the most avoidable revision rounds?
new_work: Review proposed agendas and check that summaries preserve disagreement.
Maintain brief templates, source permissions and approval roles.
Handle stale references and failed project updates.
tasks.statement: Discuss with the client the product, advertising themes and methods, and any changes that should be made in advertising copy.

tasks.short: Present draft copy and creative ideas to clients and agree the next direction.

steps.what: Assemble draft excerpts, alternatives and rationale in the {DOCS}.
Coordinate participants and a review time through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Check the review packet and share it with the client through the {EMAIL}.
Present ideas, explain trade-offs and discuss the client's reactions.
Choose a direction, request changes or defer the decision.
Write the decision, requested revisions and open questions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Writer's discussion notes and explicitly stated client decision.
loop.output: Draft review record separating decisions, requests and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link each entry to a note; writer confirms that no suggestion became an approval.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; missing decisions remain marked unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes mix commitments, reactions and suggestions in varied language.

steps.what: Send the confirmed review record and next steps through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Generate a review packet from selected material in the {DOCS}, and configure appointment booking through the {CALENDAR}. The writer approves external sharing and leads the conversation; a bounded extraction loop turns the writer's notes into a review record for confirmation and follow-up through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing packets and follow-ups meant repeated copying between documents and messages. The valuable discussion depends on trust, interpretation and negotiation.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, booking controls and version links can remove most preparation mechanics. A small extraction loop can organise notes without taking over the client conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Client reactions are often indirect, and authority to approve may be unclear. A positive reaction must not be recorded as a binding decision.
tasks.human_edge: The writer reads reactions, explains creative choices and helps the client make a decision they understand.
tasks.altitude: The writer spends more of the week discussing ideas and less assembling packets or writing follow-ups. Decision rights do not change: the client chooses the direction, and the writer confirms what was agreed.

reach.task: Present copy and visual concepts together in one coherent review.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, concept rationale and how to separate copy feedback from layout feedback.

evidence.claim: Review packets, version links, booking and notification routing can use templates and ordinary workflow configuration.
The professional writing experiment supports assistance with written preparation, not replacement of client presentations.
Distinguishing reactions from commitments remains a human judgement in this design.

assumptions: The client may be an internal requester or an external commissioner; external sharing receives an explicit writer check.
Packet generation reuses existing excerpts and concept notes rather than inventing a creative rationale.
Scheduling uses a preselected participant list and agreed booking limits.
The client decision share represents the writer's time spent obtaining that decision.
The note workflow uses written notes and does not require meeting recording.
GDPR applies to participant details and notes; access and any consultation follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether clients are internal, external or both.
Who has authority to approve concepts and scope changes.
Whether external participants can access shared material securely.
Which booking and document-sharing capabilities are already configured.
Whether the proposed note processing requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Does generated preparation improve decision clarity or merely shorten administration?
How reliably can note extraction distinguish approval, preference and an unresolved suggestion?
new_work: Maintain packet templates and booking constraints.
Check versions, recipients and access before sharing.
Confirm extracted decisions and unresolved questions.
Handle access failures, scheduling exceptions and disputed meeting records.
tasks.statement: Present drafts and ideas to clients.

tasks.short: Adapt message language and tone to the product, audience and publishing medium.

steps.what: Select audience, tone and medium requirements from the approved brief and brand guide.
Rewrite approved copy into versions suited to each audience and medium.

loop.input: Approved copy, adaptation brief, permitted claims and fixed terms.
loop.output: Copy variants with changes tracked against the approved copy.
loop.check: Check length, fixed terms, numbers and links; the writer checks tone and altered meaning.
loop.stop: Generate up to four variants and allow one repair each; unresolved meaning changes return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle dimensions and fixed terms but cannot reliably adapt nuance and tone.

steps.what: Check spelling, preferred terms, length and required wording.
Review variants for voice and meaning, then approve the selected versions.
Send approved versions and channel labels to the publishing specialist.

tasks.design: Store channel rules and approved examples in the {DOCS}; configure reusable templates and rule checks first. A bounded drafting loop creates tracked variants, and an editor approves the selected wording. The {WORKFLOW} routes approved versions to the publishing specialist with channel labels and version identifiers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tone guidance often lives in examples and editor memory, while channel constraints are scattered across documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit channel rules support deterministic checks. Bounded rewriting can produce reviewable variants without replacing the approved message.
tasks.still_hard: Humour, cultural nuance and subtle shifts in promises resist reliable automatic checking.
tasks.human_edge: The writer hears whether the message sounds credible to its audience and recognises when adaptation changes its meaning.

ambition.what: Plain-language campaign versions for readers unfamiliar with the product category.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends fewer hours repeating rewrites and more time testing whether audiences understand the message. They can propose audience treatments; final copy approval remains with the editor.

reach.task: Adapt campaign wording for page headings, forms and calls to action.
reach.learn: Content hierarchy, accessible labels and how interface context changes meaning.

evidence.claim: LanguageTool checks spelling, grammar, punctuation and style.
Acrolinx scores text against house-style guidance and supports quality gates.
Bounded tone adaptation needs human semantic review even when length and terminology checks are automatic.

assumptions: Adaptation starts from approved copy rather than generating new product claims.
Document editing dominates; the mailbox mainly carries the final handoff.
The high automation prior applies chiefly to variant drafting, not to choosing voice or approving meaning.
Build ranges cover a few channels and one language.
GDPR applies to personal data in examples. Consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether the brand guide defines usable tone rules and approved examples.
Which channels, languages and length constraints matter most.
Who approves adapted copy today.
Whether existing document tools support tracked changes and approval routing.
Which access approvals and employee consultation are required.
research_questions: Which adaptations can be handled entirely by templates and fixed substitutions?
What proportion of generated variants changes a claim or promise?
Do unfamiliar readers understand the plain-language version more accurately?
new_work: Review meaning changes and unusual tone choices.
Maintain channel limits, preferred terms and approved examples.
Resolve conflicting feedback from editors and channel owners.
Check approval routing and stale-version handling.
tasks.statement: Vary language and tone of messages based on product and medium.

tasks.short: Develop advertising campaign concepts and copy with creative, art and marketing leads.

steps.what: Discuss the campaign objective, audience, constraints and desired response.
Gather approved claims, previous campaigns, brand guidance and channel requirements.
Develop campaign concepts, narrative approaches and initial headline ideas.
Develop the strongest concept with the writer and art director.
Write channel versions and revise copy against creative feedback.

loop.input: Selected concept, approved claims, channel specifications and creative feedback.
loop.output: Channel copy drafts with claim references and tracked revisions.
loop.check: Run length, terminology and required-text checks; writer verifies claims, voice and creative fidelity.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision passes per channel; unresolved claims or weak copy return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting tone and narrative across channels requires writing beyond template substitution.

steps.what: Approve campaign copy, substantiated claims and the final creative package.
Send the approved package and production instructions to the delivery partner.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} to connect each brief to approved claims, brand guidance and channel specifications in the {DOCS}. Deterministic assembly prepares the source pack, and a bounded drafting loop adapts the human-selected concept into channel copy with rule checks and claim references. Approval records lock the final version, and the {WORKFLOW} prepares the production handover for a recipient and version check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative context, approved facts and feedback are spread across briefs and document versions. Template automation alone cannot adapt a distinctive concept across channels.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding lowers the cost of source-pack assembly, version links and channel checks. Bounded drafting can assist adaptation after people settle the creative direction.
tasks.still_hard: Original concepts, visual and verbal coherence, stakeholder disagreement and judging likely audience response remain demanding. Faster copy production does not establish campaign effectiveness.
tasks.human_edge: Creating a distinctive idea, recognising cultural meaning and developing it through collaboration.

ambition.what: Channel-ready campaign packs for small regional marketing teams.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time collecting references and reformatting copy, leaving more time for concept development and art direction. They can accept routine channel adaptations within an agreed brief; campaign approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Develop visual treatments that reinforce the campaign concept.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, copy fit and how image choices change the meaning of a headline.

reach.task: Choose channels and define a campaign test.
reach.learn: Channel economics, production constraints and testable success criteria.

evidence.claim: A trial involving 444 professionals found faster completion and better assessed quality on professional writing tasks; it did not establish campaign effectiveness.
Acrolinx provides repeatable style scoring and quality gates, supporting rule-based checks around assisted drafting.
The digest treats creative writing as human work and bounded drafting as assistance for suitable writing stages.

assumptions: The company uses an internal creative team, an external agency or both.
Approved claims and channel specifications can be identified reliably.
The delivery partner receives production materials; publishing and media spending are separate tasks.
The proposed gain is concentrated in preparation and adaptation, despite the high whole-task gain prior.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to source material and audience data. EU AI Act obligations depend on the content and use; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether the campaign archive has usable tags and current approval status.
Who approves regulated or otherwise sensitive advertising claims.
How many channels and languages each campaign requires.
Whether external partners may receive drafts or only approved materials.
Which access restrictions and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which channel adaptations preserve enough structure for deterministic templates?
Which creative feedback can be expressed as repeatable checks?
What evidence is required before a claim can enter a source pack?
new_work: Review generated channel copy and its claim references.
Maintain current brand rules, channel limits and approved claims.
Resolve conflicting feedback and unsupported wording.
Check version locks and recipients before external handover.
Assess whether extra campaign variants improve outcomes enough to justify review.
tasks.statement: Develop advertising campaigns for a wide range of clients, working with an advertising agency's creative director and art director to determine the best way to present advertising information.

tasks.short: Write articles, bulletins, sales letters, speeches and other informative or promotional material.

steps.what: Clarify the brief, intended reader and required response with the marketing manager.
Review the source pack and select evidence relevant to the writing brief.
Choose the angle, narrative structure and opening.
Draft and revise the material using the selected evidence and outline.

loop.input: Writing brief, writer-selected outline, approved evidence and brand guide.
loop.output: Copy draft with source links for factual claims and placeholders for missing evidence.
loop.check: Validate cited source identifiers, numbers and exact quotations; the writer checks narrative and claim meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and up to two repairs per item; unresolved evidence gaps block readiness and return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Long-form prose requires varied transitions and phrasing beyond fixed templates.

steps.what: Check spelling, house style, required sections and reference completeness.
Review factual accuracy, voice and permissions, then approve copy for publishing handoff.

tasks.design: Use templates and evidence links in the {DOCS} to assemble the writing brief and outline. A bounded drafting loop on the {DATA_PLATFORM} writes from selected evidence, then configured checks produce a review report. The {WORKFLOW} records editor approval and creates a publishing handoff linked to the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs, evidence and revision comments were separated, and reusable templates could not produce coherent varied prose.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can use a controlled evidence pack. Deterministic checks and approval routing make drafts easier to inspect and hand over.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive narrative, executive voice, sensitive customer stories and factual interpretation require sustained human attention.
tasks.human_edge: The writer chooses what deserves attention and creates a voice that readers recognise as credible.

ambition.what: A quarterly customer-objection explainer series grounded in verified evidence.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time producing first drafts and more time shaping angles and interviewing sources. A proposed editorial-planning remit lets them pitch the explainer series; publication approval remains with the editor.

reach.task: Explain product capabilities and limitations in customer-facing material.
reach.learn: Technical validation, version-specific facts and writing clearly about limitations.

evidence.claim: An MIT writing trial with 444 professionals reported 37% less time and a 0.45 SD quality increase; it is not a forecast for this workflow.
Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style checks and quality gates.
AI Act Article 50 addresses transparency for AI-generated public-interest text, including an editorial-review exception.
Evidence-linked drafts, templates and versioned approval routing can be combined without an autonomous agent.

assumptions: A source pack is available from the connected research task.
The baseline is document-heavy, with meetings used to clarify intent.
The high automation prior overstates replacement of angle selection, creative voice and sensitive review.
Build ranges cover selected document formats and a limited set of writing types.
GDPR applies; marketing material has no assumed journalistic exemption.
Check EU AI Act transparency duties for public-interest text. Consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which writing types account for most volume and review time.
Whether reusable briefs and source packs already exist.
Who checks technical claims, customer permissions and executive voice.
Whether any outputs fall within public-interest-text transparency duties.
Which document access and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which writing types can use templates without reducing usefulness or originality?
How often do reviewers find unsupported implications despite valid citations?
Does draft assistance reduce total time once revision and approval are included?
new_work: Review generated prose and unsupported implications.
Maintain writing templates, evidence links and approved style examples.
Route unresolved technical or permission questions to the relevant reviewer.
Maintain versioned approvals and applicable disclosure records.
tasks.statement: Write articles, bulletins, sales letters, speeches, and other related informative, marketing and promotional material.

tasks.short: Research products and interview people to choose selling features worth promoting.

steps.what: Gather product evidence, customer feedback and previous campaign findings.
Prepare questions about benefits, objections and supporting evidence.

loop.input: Research source pack, research objective and standard interview sections.
loop.output: Interview guide linked to evidence gaps and possible customer objections.
loop.check: Check required topics and source links; the writer removes leading questions and irrelevant assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision within a fixed token budget; use the standard guide if the result is unsuitable.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed guide misses questions arising from varied feedback and incomplete product evidence.

steps.what: Invite selected customers and product specialists and arrange interviews.
Interview participants and probe examples, objections and unmet needs.
Write interview notes and distinguish quotations from interpretations.

loop.input: Permitted interview recording or rough notes.
loop.output: Interview notes with source locations, attributed observations and separately marked interpretations.
loop.check: Verify quotations and important claims against the record; check attribution and flag uncertainty.
loop.stop: One transcription where available and one extraction pass within a fixed duration and token budget; unclear passages return to the interviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Speech and free-text notes require interpretation before they become structured evidence.

steps.what: Compare candidate features against audience needs, differentiation and evidence strength.
Select features and explain the proposed promotional angle.
Approve the promoted features and limits on their claims.

tasks.design: Connect approved product evidence in {DOCS} and permitted customer feedback in {CRM} to a research record in {WORKFLOW}. Configure scheduling through {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, with bounded loops for interview preparation and source-linked notes. A feature comparison in {BI} supports human selection, and the approved feature brief feeds writing projects.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback and product evidence were scattered, and interviews required trust and judgement. Recording and summarizing conversations added work without resolving which benefits mattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured retrieval and scheduling remove coordination work. Bounded transcription and extraction can prepare reviewable notes while existing records and dashboards organize evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Small interview samples can mislead, and participant statements may conflict with product evidence. Establishing demand, substantiating claims and earning candid answers remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The writer notices hesitation, asks useful follow-up questions and distinguishes a compelling benefit from a convenient marketing claim.

ambition.what: Evidence-backed objection briefs for sales teams.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more time interviewing and interpreting evidence, with less scheduling and note preparation. They can gain authority to commission follow-up interviews within an agreed budget; the marketing manager retains approval of promoted claims.

reach.task: Design a focused customer interview study.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, neutral interviewing, coding evidence and separating anecdotes from recurring patterns.

reach.task: Verify product capabilities behind proposed claims.
reach.learn: Product terminology, evidence provenance and the distinction between demonstrated capability and planned functionality.

evidence.claim: Amberscript provides machine transcription and human-checked output; its advertised accuracy does not guarantee accuracy for these interviews.
Full Fact AI flags checkable claims and matches repeated claims; this supports triage rather than proof of product benefits.
The documented invented-quotation incident supports checking quotations against original records.
The proposed research workflow, time shares and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The writer researches commercial product messages rather than conducting purely journalistic interviews.
A feature comparison often uses a spreadsheet to combine evidence from different sources.
The high prior that the task vanishes is rejected: interviews and feature selection remain necessary.
Recording is optional; participants receive appropriate information, and records use an established lawful basis and retention policy.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations apply; national rules govern employee consultation where relevant.
The access estimate includes recording arrangements and employee consultation where required; elapsed approval time can be longer.
unknowns: Whether customer feedback may be reused for this research purpose.
Whether interviews may be recorded and processed in the available environment.
How participants are selected and whether important groups are missing.
Who substantiates product claims and approves quotations for external use.
Which retention, access and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which extraction checks best preserve uncertainty and disagreement in interview notes?
When does a structured feature comparison improve selection without creating false numerical precision?
new_work: Review interview guides for leading questions.
Verify quotations, attributions and uncertain transcript passages.
Maintain access controls, retention settings and recording permissions.
Update feature evidence and resolve conflicting sources.
Maintain scheduling connections and comparison criteria.
tasks.statement: Conduct research and interviews to determine which of a product's selling features should be promoted.

tasks.short: Invent product names and slogans, then assess fit, language risks and legal clearance.

steps.what: Read the naming brief, product facts, audience needs and brand constraints.
Generate alternative product names and slogans across several creative directions.

loop.input: Naming criteria, approved product facts, brand terms and excluded names.
loop.output: A grouped longlist of names and slogans with short rationales.
loop.check: Check duplicates, length, excluded terms and unsupported product claims; writer reviews originality and fit.
loop.stop: Two batches of at most 25 candidates and one revision batch; writer continues manually if no direction is useful.
loop.why_not_simpler: Novel wording and associations cannot be produced adequately by fixed substitution rules.

steps.what: Develop and shortlist candidates for meaning, memorability, distinctiveness and audience fit.
Check shortlisted wording against existing names, excluded terms and format limits.
Check pronunciation, unintended meanings and cultural suitability in target languages.
Assess trademark conflicts and clearance needs using the {OTHER} trademark registry.
Approve the chosen name and slogan for the specified markets and uses.

tasks.design: A reusable naming form in the {WORKFLOW} assembles product facts and naming criteria from the {DOCS}. A bounded generator proposes candidates, while deterministic checks flag duplicates, excluded terms and format failures against the {DOCS} and {CMS}. The writer develops the shortlist, specialists assess language and legal risks, and the marketing manager approves a specific name and use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates can check constraints but offer little useful variety. Generating candidates has been mixed with the harder work of selecting and clearing them.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded generation can supply varied starting points cheaply. AI coding makes a small candidate record, repeatable constraint checks and a review pack economical.
tasks.still_hard: Memorable originality, cultural meaning and legal clearance remain uncertain. A registry search or absence of an exact match does not establish trademark availability.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a name people will remember, improving weak ideas and judging cultural and commercial consequences.

ambition.what: A naming review pack covering creative rationale, language risks and clearance status.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time producing an initial longlist and checking mechanical constraints. They take a stronger role in developing and explaining naming choices; legal clearance and final approval remain with the relevant roles.

reach.task: Assess a proposed name across target languages.
reach.learn: Pronunciation checks, local connotations and when native-market review is needed.

reach.task: Test shortlisted names and slogans on packaging and promotional layouts.
reach.learn: Visual word shape, reading distance and physical space constraints.

evidence.claim: Assisted professional writing has documented productivity benefits, but the trial does not establish naming originality or trademark safety.
Acrolinx demonstrates repeatable terminology and style checks that can support mechanical candidate screening.
Generating name candidates is feasible; selecting distinctive names and assessing legal conflicts require separate judgement.

assumptions: The workflow is for product names and slogans, rather than full brand strategy.
Language review applies to the intended markets; some cases require only one language.
Registry searches support specialist assessment and do not constitute automated clearance.
The near-total automation prior is too strong: candidate production changes substantially, while selection and clearance remain human.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to any personal data in briefs. EU AI Act obligations depend on use; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which markets, languages and product categories require clearance.
Whether existing names and excluded terms are maintained centrally.
Who can approve a name and accept residual legal risk.
Whether confidential launch information may enter the approved model environment.
Whether access changes trigger consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which naming constraints can be enforced through existing document templates or forms?
Do generated candidates add useful diversity compared with the writer's current process?
What evidence must accompany a clearance recommendation for each target market?
new_work: Review generated candidates for derivative wording and unsupported claims.
Maintain existing-name lists, excluded terms and naming criteria.
Coordinate language and legal checks for shortlisted candidates.
Record approval scope and restrictions so later uses do not exceed clearance.
Remove weak candidate batches instead of expanding the review queue indefinitely.
tasks.statement: Invent names for products and write the slogans that appear on packaging, brochures and other promotional material.

tasks.short: Use advertising trends, consumer research and campaign results to recommend promotional approaches.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, promotional question and commercial constraints with the marketing manager.
Collect campaign results, survey reports and relevant advertising examples.
Align periods, audience definitions and campaign metrics in a comparison workbook.
Read survey findings and examples, recording themes, evidence and limitations.

loop.input: Selected survey reports and advertising examples with source dates and research questions.
loop.output: Evidence notes linking each theme to a passage, sample and stated limitation.
loop.check: Verify references and quoted figures; writer checks interpretation and contradictory evidence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per source; unresolved claims remain flagged and excluded from recommendations.
loop.why_not_simpler: Themes and limitations appear in varied prose and cannot be recovered through metric rules alone.

steps.what: Compare promotional options and write a recommendation with an explicit test hypothesis.
Agree the promotional approach, test limits and success criteria.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers approved exports from the {ADS}, {SOCIAL}, {BI} and {DOCS}, then calculates comparable metrics and flags mismatches. A bounded loop turns selected reports into cited evidence notes beside a {BI} comparison. The writer recommends a test, and the marketing manager approves its limits before campaign execution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports use different periods and audience definitions. Gathering evidence and rebuilding comparisons consumes time before interpretation starts.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic connectors and metric rules can handle repeatable preparation. Bounded reading can produce source-linked notes without pretending to establish causality.
tasks.still_hard: Survey bias, attribution gaps and changing audience behaviour limit conclusions. A persuasive pattern may still fail in a live campaign.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a commercially useful question and deciding which imperfect evidence deserves a test.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one message hypothesis for a limited campaign test.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more time interpreting evidence and proposing tests. If the marketing manager delegates a defined test allowance, the writer can choose message hypotheses within it; budget expansion remains a separate decision.

reach.task: Assess whether survey findings support a campaign hypothesis.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, comparable audience definitions and the difference between association and causal evidence.

reach.task: Translate a message hypothesis into a measurable campaign test.
reach.learn: Test design, attribution limits and stopping criteria.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides conversation and news monitoring, supporting configured collection of trend signals.
Archive question answering is being tested, supporting the feasibility of source-grounded research assistance.
Metric alignment and dashboard preparation can use deterministic transformations; promotional judgement remains context-dependent.

assumptions: The writer uses existing research and campaign data rather than commissioning a new survey in every case.
The comparison workbook bridges reports whose definitions are currently inconsistent.
Remaining recommendation time falls because evidence is prepared, while the decision remains human.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to consumer data; the design favours aggregate findings and approved access. Consultation under national rules is included where applicable.
unknowns: Which campaign and survey sources are licensed and accessible.
Whether audience and conversion definitions can be aligned.
Whether survey text includes personal or sensitive information.
Who may approve tests and what spending limits can be delegated.
Which employee consultation requirements apply to the implementation.
research_questions: Which research questions recur often enough to justify scheduled collection?
Which metric mismatches should block comparison instead of being normalised?
Can existing reporting configuration replace a custom dashboard?
new_work: Review source-linked findings and contradictory evidence.
Maintain metric definitions, source permissions and collection schedules.
Investigate missing data and changes in source formats.
Record test outcomes so later recommendations can use actual results.
tasks.statement: Review advertising trends, consumer surveys, and other data regarding marketing of goods and services to determine the best way to promote products.

tasks.short: Coordinate and co-write project material with other writers.

steps.what: Agree the outline, section owners, voice and deadlines with other writers.
Write assigned sections and comment on colleagues' drafts.
Email document copies and collect revised versions from contributors.
Consolidate tracked revisions into a comparison draft.
Resolve disagreements about structure, argument, voice and conflicting edits.
Approve the combined manuscript for the next production stage.

tasks.design: Configure a shared manuscript in the {DOCS} with section ownership, tracked changes, comments and version history, linked to deadlines in the {PROJECT}. Contributors work in that record, removing attachment exchange and manual revision assembly. The editor records approval in the {WORKFLOW} before the manuscript moves to production.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attachment habits, unclear section ownership and inconsistent access keep collaboration fragmented. The underlying version-control and review features often already exist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration can remove much of the coordination work immediately. Coding assistance can cheaply connect project status where configuration alone is insufficient; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Shared editing does not resolve incompatible arguments, uneven voice or interpersonal tension. Contributors may also work outside the shared workspace.
tasks.human_edge: Writers negotiate meaning, preserve useful differences in voice and make a coherent piece from several perspectives.

ambition.what: Support occasional subject-matter contributors who do not normally join multi-writer projects.

tasks.altitude: The lead writer spends less time collecting versions and more time coaching contributors and shaping the manuscript. Section coordination can expand with delegation; final editorial approval remains assigned to the editor.

reach.task: Shape the structure and continuity of a multi-author manuscript.
reach.learn: Structural editing, constructive feedback and techniques for reconciling different voices.

reach.task: Prepare a consistent manuscript handoff for layout.
reach.learn: Document styles, asset references and production-ready file requirements.

evidence.claim: Shared documents, tracked changes and version history can replace attachment circulation and revision assembly.
Coordination improvements do not establish that original co-writing or editorial disagreement can be automated.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates; teams already using shared editing have less to save.

assumptions: A mixed workflow of shared documents and emailed revisions is typical for the baseline described.
The {DOCS} supports tracked changes, permissions and version comparison.
Revision assembly preserves proposed edits; it does not automatically accept conflicting changes.
Original writing remains human, consistent with the substantial creation share in the supplied priors.
GDPR applies to contributor records. This design adds no model processing or employee productivity scoring.

Does section ownership improve delivery without fragmenting the manuscript's overall argument?

Maintain document templates and notification settings.

Coach occasional contributors in tracked changes and editorial review.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with other writers on specific projects.

tasks.short: Research facts and authentic details for marketing writing through documents, records and interviews.

steps.what: Define research questions and the evidence needed for the approved brief.
Search the {DOCS} and public pages for relevant source material.
Read sources and record useful facts, quotations and provenance.

loop.input: Retrieved source passages with document identifiers and locations.
loop.output: Research notes linking each fact and quotation to its source passage.
loop.check: Validate source locations and exact quotations; the writer checks meaning and relevance.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per source, capped at 20 sources; unreadable material returns to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free text expresses relevant facts in varied forms; search rules cannot extract their meaning reliably.

steps.what: Interview a subject expert or customer to resolve gaps and obtain authentic details.
Resolve conflicting accounts and decide which claims and quotations are usable.
Assemble the source pack with citations, approved claims and unresolved gaps.

tasks.design: Configure search in the {DOCS}, with saved queries and source metadata. A bounded extraction loop on the {DATA_PLATFORM} drafts cited notes, while a deterministic generator assembles the source pack from the writer-approved claim register. Interviews and decisions about conflicting evidence stay with the writer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources differ in format, provenance is recorded manually, and missing details require access to people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and document metadata cover retrieval. Bounded extraction can reduce note-taking, and AI-assisted coding can shorten implementation of citation checks.
tasks.still_hard: Source access, contradictory evidence, contextual quotation and securing candid interviews remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: The writer notices what is missing, earns trust and distinguishes authentic detail from a convenient marketing claim.

ambition.what: A reusable customer-story evidence pack with verified quotations and explicit usage permissions.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time copying passages and more time interviewing and investigating weak claims. They gain a proposed right to flag unsupported claims for escalation before drafting.

reach.task: Turn customer interviews into evidence about buying barriers.
reach.learn: Interview sampling, question bias and the difference between an anecdote and a supported finding.

evidence.claim: Archive question answering is being tested; this supports retrieval assistance, not automatic acceptance of answers.
Full Fact AI flags checkable claims and matches repeated claims; it does not establish every claim's truth.
Invented quotations are a documented failure; quotation provenance requires explicit checking.
Search configuration and deterministic source-pack assembly are feasible with structured source metadata.

assumptions: The baseline is a marketing writer in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Documents and interviews dominate the task; search still requires human source selection.
Build ranges describe a limited pilot using accessible documents, not a complete external archive.
GDPR applies to customer and employee information. Marketing research has no assumed journalistic exemption.
Employee consultation follows national rules where applicable; individual productivity monitoring is outside this design.

Whether interviewees have agreed to recording, quotation and marketing use.

Can reviewers trace every extracted quotation to an exact source location?
How much time is spent collecting notes versus resolving contradictory accounts?

Maintain source permissions, retention settings and access restrictions.
Resolve unreadable documents and conflicting claims.
Maintain the source-pack template and extraction checks.
tasks.statement: Conduct research to obtain factual information and authentic detail, using sources such as newspaper accounts, diaries, and interviews.

tasks.short: Gather product facts and agree advertising style, length and channel requirements with representatives.

steps.what: Find current product information and existing channel specifications.
Request missing facts and specifications from sales, media and marketing representatives.
Discuss product nuances, audience needs, tone and channel constraints with representatives.
Combine consultation notes and source documents into writing requirements.

loop.input: Consultation notes, versioned product information and channel specifications.
loop.output: Writing requirements and proposed claims with source references and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Check required fields, source versions and exact limits; writer reviews interpretations and contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; unresolved facts are routed to their named owners.
loop.why_not_simpler: Channel limits are structured, but product qualifications and intended tone often appear in free text.

steps.what: Confirm factual claims and product qualifications before they become approved writing inputs.
Copy confirmed requirements into a separate handoff document for the creative team.

tasks.design: A structured brief in the {WORKFLOW} links versioned product facts and channel specifications in the {DOCS}, requesting only missing required fields. A bounded loop turns consultation notes into proposed requirements and a source-linked claim register for writer review and product-owner approval. The creative team uses that approved record directly.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product facts have different owners, and channel requirements arrive in inconsistent documents. The writer repeatedly asks people to explain context and confirm versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic completeness checks can route routine requests, while a small extraction loop handles narrative qualifications. Coding assistance reduces the cost of connecting these records.
tasks.still_hard: A document reference does not prove a claim is true. Conflicting commercial priorities and undocumented product limitations still need accountable people.
tasks.human_edge: The writer asks the question that exposes an overclaim and translates specialist explanations into audience-relevant meaning.

ambition.what: Offer a pre-draft claim-readiness review for campaign briefs.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time chasing facts and more time identifying claims that need evidence or qualification. The writer can recommend readiness; the product owner retains factual approval.

reach.task: Maintain reusable explanations of product capabilities and limitations.
reach.learn: Source versioning, controlled terminology and precise qualification of technical claims.

reach.task: Translate a campaign brief into channel-specific copy requirements.
reach.learn: Search intent, format limits and how landing-page promises connect to advertising copy.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, completeness checks and version-linked records can handle routine information gathering.
Full Fact AI demonstrates claim identification and repeat matching, not automatic validation of product claims.
House-style checking is available, but cannot replace agreement about intended audience and tone.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The company has identifiable owners for product facts and channel requirements.
Routine requests go to internal representatives; external media commitments require a separate authorised action.
Representatives still supply missing facts. Their work is not counted as eliminated writer time.
The conversation remains substantial, consistent with the supplied human-work prior.
GDPR applies to personal data. Applicable EU AI Act duties and national rules must be assessed for the actual deployment.
Access estimates include any required employee consultation; a formal process may exceed the range.
unknowns: Which product records are authoritative, and who approves each claim category?
How often do product facts or channel specifications change?
Can the {DOCS} provide reliable version identifiers and access controls?

Which required fields reduce clarification rounds without creating unnecessary work for representatives?
new_work: Maintain fact ownership, required fields and channel specifications.
Review extracted qualifications and resolve contradictory sources.
Reapprove affected claims when source material changes.
Handle missing inputs and prevent outdated approved records from being reused.
tasks.statement: Consult with sales, media and marketing representatives to obtain information on product or service and discuss style and length of advertising written material.

tasks.short: Edit existing copy and submit a controlled version for editorial approval.

steps.what: Find the latest manuscript and instructions in the {EMAIL} and {DOCS}.
Edit or rewrite the working manuscript in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Canonical manuscript version, revision brief, approved sources and protected text.
loop.output: Tracked edit proposals restricted to the requested scope.
loop.check: Validate unchanged protected text and source references; writer reviews meaning and substantive changes.
loop.stop: One edit pass and one repair pass; unresolved passages return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Mechanical corrections use rules, but scoped restructuring and rewriting need contextual language judgement.

steps.what: Check the revised manuscript against the brief, sources and style guide.
Prepare the version, change record and supporting material in the {DOCS}.
Submit the approval packet to the editor through the {EMAIL}.
Review the submitted version in the {DOCS} and approve or return it.
Record the editorial decision and next action in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Use a canonical manuscript in the {DOCS} to eliminate version hunting, and configure style checks before a bounded editing loop proposes substantive changes. Deterministic code builds a version-specific approval packet; the {WORKFLOW} routes it to the editor and updates the {PROJECT} after an explicit decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval evidence was split across manuscript versions, messages and status records. Language tools corrected mechanics but did not connect a substantive revision to a specific approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing version controls and approval functions handle routing and records. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting them, while bounded editing supplies reviewable proposals.
tasks.still_hard: Editorial responsibility cannot be reduced to a style score. Late changes must invalidate approval, and a source-linked passage can still mislead or infringe rights.
tasks.human_edge: The writer preserves intended meaning, and the editor decides whether the complete manuscript is fit for its audience and purpose.

ambition.what: A lightweight editorial review service for regional event teams.

tasks.altitude: The writer handles fewer version searches and approval chases, leaving more time for difficult edits and support to occasional contributors. The writer can return incomplete submissions against agreed criteria; the editor retains acceptance authority.

reach.task: Triage submissions for completeness and route sensitive claims for specialist review.
reach.learn: Editorial risk categories, escalation criteria and version-specific approval controls.

evidence.claim: Acrolinx supports repeatable style assessment and quality gates.
LanguageTool supports mechanical language checks before substantive editorial review.
The digest reports invented quotations in published AI-assisted writing, supporting explicit source and quotation review.
Version-specific routing, deterministic change records and approval invalidation can use standard configuration and code.

assumptions: This task concerns a controlled editorial submission; publication is a separate action.
Substantive revision here uses an agreed brief; negotiation of that brief belongs to the revision task.
The {DOCS} exposes stable version identifiers and the {PROJECT} supports status updates.
The editor review share represents the writer's task time spent in the approval exchange; editor effort needs separate capacity planning.
Approval applies only to the reviewed version and is invalidated by subsequent substantive edits.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations remain relevant; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Build ranges cover working effort, including initial access and consultation work, rather than statutory waiting periods.

Which changes require renewed approval.

Review substantive edit proposals and source-sensitive passages.
Handle returned submissions and missing supporting evidence.
Monitor version mismatches, failed status updates and stale approvals.
tasks.statement: Edit or rewrite existing written material as necessary, and submit written material for approval by supervisor, editor, or publisher.

tasks.short: Confirm copyright ownership and obtain missing permissions for completed work.

steps.what: List contributors, borrowed material and existing permissions for the completed work.

loop.input: Completed work, contributor agreements and existing permission records.
loop.output: Draft rights inventory with document references and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; writer checks uncertain attribution and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or ambiguous documents go to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contributor terms and permissions often sit in free text with inconsistent wording.

steps.what: Determine ownership, missing permissions and whether any formal procedure is needed.
Prepare permission requests and supporting evidence using approved templates.
Send approved permission requests and follow up with rights holders.
Resolve permission conditions, fees and restrictions before accepting terms.
File permissions and record attribution, permitted uses and expiry dates.

tasks.design: Configure a rights register in the {CLM} or {DOCS}, linked to completed work and contributor agreements. A bounded extraction loop prepares the inventory, while deterministic templates and the {WORKFLOW} prepare requests, track replies and record approved permissions. The legal adviser determines the route, eliminates unnecessary applications and approves requests and commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rights evidence is scattered across documents and correspondence. Ownership and permitted use cannot be inferred safely from a completed manuscript.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and approval features cover much of the process. AI coding makes document assembly and record links cheaper; bounded extraction reduces manual reading.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed ownership, negotiated licences and territorial differences remain legal work. Copyright generally arises automatically for eligible original work; registration or other procedures depend on the relevant national rules and intended use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertain ownership, negotiating fair terms and accepting legal responsibility.

ambition.what: A searchable catalogue of material cleared for reuse, with usage restrictions.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time assembling evidence and chasing replies. With delegated authority, they can select already-cleared material within recorded limits; new legal commitments remain with the authorised approver.

reach.task: Check rights readiness before publication.
reach.learn: Translate permission conditions into attribution instructions and publication checks.

evidence.claim: Rights inventories, template assembly and approval routing are feasible with document and workflow capabilities.
Copyright protection generally arises automatically for eligible original work; permissions and ownership still need checking.
The digest's text-and-data-mining provision does not establish permission to republish third-party material.

assumptions: The typical task concerns ownership evidence and permissions, rather than routine copyright registration.
The legal adviser may be internal or retained externally.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
GDPR applies to contributor and contact data. Access review is included; employee consultation depends on the change and national rules.

Keep rights records aligned with later revisions and new publication uses.

tasks.short: Plan a writing project, develop its outline and organize the supporting material.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, purpose, deliverables and deadline with the requester.
Find and group source material for the project.
Arrange the material into an outline with sections and supporting points.

loop.input: Content brief, format template and linked source material.
loop.output: Draft outline with section purposes, supporting sources and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections, source identifiers and brief coverage. The writer assesses narrative order during outline review.
loop.stop: Generate at most two outline alternatives and one repair pass within a fixed token budget; return unresolved gaps to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates define sections but cannot consistently organize varied source narratives around a new brief.

steps.what: Review the proposed structure and agree the scope with the requester.
Set writing, design and review milestones in the project plan.
Copy the agreed outline and milestones into a status email.

tasks.design: Link a structured brief in {PROJECT} to approved material in {DOCS}, and use a bounded loop to propose an outline. After scope approval, configure milestone templates and dependency checks in {PROJECT}. Shared plan views and configured notifications remove the separate status email.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative structure depended on judgement, while source folders and project schedules were disconnected. A standard project template could not produce a useful outline from varied material.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can propose source-linked structures, while configured project templates handle milestones. Small integrations can connect document references and project records.
tasks.still_hard: A coherent outline can still pursue the wrong story. Negotiating scope, resource conflicts and stakeholder priorities remains human work.
tasks.human_edge: The writer identifies the central idea, removes attractive distractions and negotiates a realistic scope.

ambition.what: Reassess narrative structure when new source evidence arrives.

tasks.altitude: The writer reviews structures and evidence gaps instead of repeatedly sorting files and copying plans. With delegated limits, they can reorder sections and adjust writing milestones without reopening the whole brief.

reach.task: Assess structural coherence before drafting starts.
reach.learn: Argument structure, narrative pacing and how to separate evidence gaps from stylistic choices.

reach.task: Plan visual assets alongside the outline.
reach.learn: Visual storytelling, asset lead times and production dependencies.

The professional-writing trial supports bounded writing assistance, but did not establish results for narrative outlining specifically.
Creative structure and stakeholder scope decisions remain judgement-dependent.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for a limited initial implementation.

Approved sources have campaign or project metadata; poorly indexed archives need additional preparation.
The automation prior applies mainly to preparation, outline proposals and administration.
Schedule suggestions use existing capacity information and flag conflicts rather than resolve them automatically.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations apply.

Which project templates and review dependencies already exist.
Who can approve scope and milestone changes.
Whether resource availability is recorded reliably.
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply.

Maintain brief templates, source metadata and milestone dependencies.
Resolve scheduling conflicts and scope exceptions.

tasks.statement: Plan project arrangements or outlines, and organize material accordingly.

tasks.short: Format approved work, assemble the publication package and submit it to a publisher or producer.

steps.what: Find the recipient's format, submission requirements and deadline.
Apply the required layout, file format and naming convention.
Assemble the work, assets, credits and rights records.
Preview the package and check completeness, layout and version.
Authorize the package, recipient and submission timing.
Send the package and record the submission receipt.

tasks.design: Store recipient requirements in {WORKFLOW} and generate publication packages from approved material in {DOCS}. Validate files, required assets and versions, then send through {EMAIL} after approval of the exact package and destination; record receipts in {PROJECT}. The authorization step supplies the transmission gate, and any package or destination change invalidates it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipients used different formats, and requirements lived in messages. Manual packaging was easier than maintaining separate export routines.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval flows cover submission control. Small deterministic exporters and validators are cheaper to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: One-off production formats, ambiguous rights records and inaccessible submission portals require manual exceptions. Receipt of a package does not mean acceptance for publication.
tasks.human_edge: The writer judges whether a package meets the producer's expectations and resolves unusual editorial requests.

ambition.what: Publication-ready partner content packages with credits and rights records.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time exporting and chasing versions, and more time resolving production exceptions. They can gain authority to select validated output formats; submission approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Prepare production-ready layouts.
reach.learn: Typography, layout specifications, accessibility and export validation.

reach.task: Coordinate a timed partner release.
reach.learn: Embargo handling, recipient requirements and publication acknowledgement.

Acrolinx provides text quality gates, supporting one component of package checking rather than the full submission process.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.

tasks.short: Revise manuscripts to meet the writer's standards and stakeholder needs.

steps.what: Collect stakeholder comments and attachments from the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Comments tied to a specific manuscript version.
loop.output: Revision list linking each request to its author and passage, with conflicts flagged.
loop.check: Every comment must be represented or explicitly marked unclear; preserve original wording and links.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass; ambiguous or conflicting requests go to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text requests express intent and contradictions that exact matching cannot reliably group.

steps.what: Resolve conflicting feedback and agree priorities with the marketing manager.
Read the manuscript in the {DOCS} and choose substantive changes.
Rewrite selected passages and restructure the manuscript in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Versioned manuscript, selected revision instructions, protected passages and approved sources.
loop.output: Tracked revision proposals with each change linked to an instruction.
loop.check: Check protected text, names, numbers and quotations; writer assesses meaning, structure and voice.
loop.stop: One proposal and one repair pass per selected passage; unresolved changes remain manual.
loop.why_not_simpler: Substantive restructuring and tone changes cannot be expressed as fixed replacements.

steps.what: Check language, factual changes and final fit in the {DOCS}.
Circulate the revised version and change record through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Keep one manuscript in the {DOCS}, with version-linked comments and revision routing in the {WORKFLOW}. Small bounded loops organise free-text feedback and propose selected rewrites; configured language checks support the writer's acceptance review before internal circulation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comments arrived against different versions, and substantive changes depended on unwritten preferences. Basic proofreading could help, but it could not resolve competing intentions.
tasks.enabler_now: Version controls and configurable checks already handle mechanical work. Small custom connectors and bounded rewriting make it practical to preserve comment provenance and propose changes in context.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders can disagree about the audience, promise or tone. A fluent rewrite can alter a qualification or weaken a deliberate creative choice.
tasks.human_edge: The writer judges which changes improve the work and negotiates requests that would damage its purpose or credibility.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a clearer message variant for audience testing.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time collating feedback and making routine rewrites, and more time resolving intent and comparing alternatives. The writer selects revisions within the approved brief; the marketing manager authorises audience tests.

reach.task: Frame a message comparison with a clear audience question and success measure.
reach.learn: Test design, sampling bias and how to interpret uncertain results.

LanguageTool checks language and offers rephrasing support.
Professional writing experiments support potential drafting gains, but do not establish savings for conflicting stakeholder revisions.
Version-linked comments, protected passages and approval routing can be implemented with ordinary configuration and code.

tasks.short: Develop script, story and advertising concepts with colleagues.

steps.what: Review the brief, audience research, product information and previous creative work.

loop.input: Approved brief and selected, permissioned research and archive material.
loop.output: Source-linked audience tensions, constraints and open questions.
loop.check: Verify citations and brief coverage; writer checks interpretations against the original material.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; unsupported interpretations are removed or marked as questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules assemble sources, but research findings and creative constraints are expressed in free text.

steps.what: Explore narrative directions and challenge ideas with colleagues.
Write original treatments, sample lines or script outlines for shortlisted concepts.
Check treatments against length limits, required elements and house style.
Choose the concept to develop and record the rationale.
Share the selected treatment and update the creative project.

tasks.design: A template in the {DOCS} combines the approved brief with source-linked research, using a bounded extraction loop for preparation. Configured checks flag length, terminology and required-element issues while people develop original treatments and choose a direction. A selection recorded in the {WORKFLOW} updates the {PROJECT} and shares the treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative material is loosely structured, and useful concepts depend on taste and shared context. Manual preparation and repeated checking surround that creative work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing style checks and inexpensive brief assembly can remove preparation work. Bounded extraction makes research easier to inspect without requiring autonomous concept selection.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, humour, cultural meaning and production feasibility resist reliable scoring. Familiar archive material can also narrow the team's ideas.

Keeping original creative development human while automating preparation is a design judgement.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.

The creative archive is permissioned and contains material the team may reuse for reference.

tasks.statement: Work with staff to develop script, story, or advertising concepts.

tasks.short: Write advertising copy for publication, broadcast and online campaigns that promote goods and services.

steps.what: Clarify the campaign objective, audience, offer and media requirements.
Develop the creative proposition, hook and call to action.
Write headlines, body copy and scripts for the selected advertising concept.

loop.input: Writer-selected concept, offer terms, approved claims and media constraints.
loop.output: Advertising drafts grouped by medium, with claim references and fixed offer terms.
loop.check: Check length, required wording, prices and claim identifiers; the writer checks persuasion and implied promises.
loop.stop: Generate up to six drafts with one repair each; unsupported claims or persistent failures return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard offers, but expressive headlines and scripts require flexible language.

steps.what: Check media limits, spelling, offer details and required disclaimers.
Check explicit and implied claims against evidence; escalate uncertain wording.
Approve advertising wording after resolving claim-review issues.
Send approved copy and media specifications to the campaign specialist.

tasks.design: Keep approved offers, claim evidence and channel rules in the {DOCS}, with deterministic templates for standard advertisements. A bounded drafting loop produces copy for writer-selected concepts, and deterministic checks flag constraint violations before manager approval. An integration creates approved-copy drafts in the {ADS} and production handoffs in the {PROJECT}; campaign activation remains a separate action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer terms, evidence and media constraints were maintained separately, while creative copy resisted fixed templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured offer records and constraint checks handle repeatable work. Bounded drafting helps expand a chosen concept into reviewable executions.
tasks.still_hard: Original concepts, implied claims, regulated categories and coordinating wording with visuals or performance remain demanding.
tasks.human_edge: The writer understands what will persuade without overstating the offer and judges how copy and visuals combine.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of the next advertising-message hypothesis to test.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time resizing copy and more time developing concepts and interpreting campaign evidence. They gain a proposed right to select message hypotheses within the approved campaign brief; budget and activation stay with the campaign owner.

reach.learn: Experiment design, attribution limits and the difference between clicks and qualified demand.

reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, image rights and how layout changes an offer's interpretation.

evidence.claim: House-style scoring and quality gates are available through Acrolinx.
The MIT trial supports assisted professional writing, but does not establish advertising conversion gains.
Fixed offer terms, length limits and draft handoffs can be handled deterministically; implied claims require review.

assumptions: The baseline covers writing and production handoff, not media buying or campaign activation.

tasks.design: Configure brief templates, source filters and style checks in the {DOCS}; use the {WORKFLOW} to route checked manuscripts. tasks.previous_blocker: Source material was scattered, and bespoke creative choices could not be reduced to templates. Connecting source references, version records and review routing required custom work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, templates and review controls cover much of the support work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, and bounded drafting can handle selected explanatory passages.
tasks.still_hard: Original voice, narrative coherence and accurate implications require close reading. Source links do not prove that a claim follows from a source, and quotation or reuse rights still need attention.
